dimensions.name: Cyclomatic Complexity
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How tangled the control flow is — methods with many branches are hard to test and change.

dimensions.name: Cognitive Complexity
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How hard the code is for a person to follow, beyond raw branching.

dimensions.name: God Classes
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Over-large classes that try to do too much ("god classes").

dimensions.name: Code Duplication
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Copy-pasted code that should be shared instead.

dimensions.name: Coupling
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether volatile projects sit underneath others that depend on them (so their churn ripples upward), and whether project dependencies form cycles. A widely-depended-on but stable shared/kernel project is healthy, not penalised.

dimensions.name: Cohesion (LCOM4)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a class's methods are focused on a single responsibility.

dimensions.name: Architectural Integrity
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the code respects its intended layering / architecture rules.

dimensions.name: Code Coverage
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How much of the code is actually exercised by tests.

dimensions.name: Test Distribution
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the test suite has a healthy mix of unit / integration / end-to-end tests.

dimensions.name: Test Quality
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the tests truly assert behaviour rather than just running the code.

dimensions.name: Test Reliability
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the tests pass reliably, with no flakiness.

dimensions.name: Dependency Hygiene
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether dependencies are current, secure, and not bloated.

dimensions.name: Secret Scanning
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether any secrets (keys, tokens, passwords) have leaked into the code.

dimensions.name: License Compliance
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the licenses of third-party packages are compatible with your policy.

dimensions.name: Churn × Complexity Hotspots
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Files that change often and are also complex — the riskiest hotspots.

dimensions.name: Bus Factor
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether knowledge is concentrated in too few people (the "bus factor").

dimensions.name: Explicit Debt
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Acknowledged debt left in the code — TODOs, dead code, suppressed warnings.

dimensions.name: Solution Shape
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the solution is laid out in a sensible, conventional structure.

dimensions.name: Documentation Quality
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the project's documentation is clear, complete, and useful.

dimensions.name: ADR Quality
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether architecture decisions are recorded well (context, decision, consequences).

dimensions.name: Naming Consistency
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether names — types, methods, variables — are clear and consistent.

dimensions.name: Internal API Consistency
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the internal API surface is consistent and coherent.

dimensions.name: Boundary Type-Coupling
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether domain types (IDs, enums, value objects) leak across bounded-context boundaries.

dimensions.name: Comment Value
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether comments are worth it — explaining WHY (valuable) rather than WHAT (redundant).

dimensions.name: ADR Conformance
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the code actually follows the decisions recorded in the project's ADRs.

dimensions.name: Project Cohesion
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether each project is a focused, coherent unit rather than an oversized grab-bag.

dimensions.name: Navigability
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How far you must trace to follow a call — low indirection and co-located slices read easier.

dimensions.name: Secrets (history)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether any secrets were ever committed — scanned across the full git history, not just now.

dimensions.name: Static Analysis (SAST)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Real static-analysis (SAST) findings — likely security bugs in the code, any language.

dimensions.name: Dependency Vulnerabilities
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether any dependency has a known published vulnerability (CVE), direct or transitive, in ANY ecosystem the repository declares — Dart pub, Elixir and Erlang via Hex, Go modules, Java and Kotlin via Maven/Gradle, JavaScript/npm, .NET/NuGet, PHP/Composer, Python/PyPI, RubyGems, Rust/Cargo and Swift.

dimensions.name: IaC & Container Security
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether Dockerfiles / Terraform / Kubernetes config follow security best practices.

dimensions.name: Data Compliance (PII/GDPR)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Likely personal-data (PII / GDPR) handling concerns — logging or storing data without safeguards.

dimensions.name: Knowledge Freshness
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether anyone still has living knowledge of each file, or it has been orphaned — last understood long ago by someone now gone quiet. The sibling of the bus factor: D16 asks who owns it, D34 asks whether anyone still knows it.

dimensions.name: Change Coupling
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether files that change together actually belong together — pairs that repeatedly co-change in git history despite having no explicit code dependency, surfacing the hidden/logical coupling (and boundaries in the wrong place) a static scan can't see.

dimensions.name: Supply-chain Provenance & Signing
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the build pipeline provides supply-chain integrity — generated provenance/attestation, signed artifacts (cosign/sigstore), an SBOM, and pinned build actions. Presence of the configuration, not a runtime guarantee.

dimensions.name: Vulnerability-disclosure Policy
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the repository publishes a coordinated-vulnerability-disclosure policy (SECURITY.md or security.txt) with a reporting contact, so finders know how to report a vulnerability. Presence of a policy file with a contact, not whether the policy is adequate or honoured.

dimensions.name: IL Efficiency
dimensions.whatItMeasures: IL Efficiency

dimensions.name: Network Egress Confinement
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether Kubernetes workloads restrict network EGRESS with a NetworkPolicy (or Cilium policy), limiting where a compromised pod can send data or reach a command-and-control server. Presence of committed egress-restricting policy, not runtime enforcement.

dimensions.name: Kernel & Syscall Confinement
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether Kubernetes workloads confine the kernel boundary — a seccomp profile (RuntimeDefault/Localhost) plus an AppArmor/SELinux mandatory-access-control layer — shrinking the syscall attack surface a container escape would use. Presence of committed confinement config, not runtime enforcement.

dimensions.name: Runtime Threat Enforcement
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the Kubernetes deployment wires runtime threat enforcement — a detection engine (Tetragon/Falco) and/or an admission-control policy gate (Kyverno / OPA Gatekeeper / PodSecurity). Presence of committed policy, not a runtime guarantee.

dimensions.name: Malicious Dependencies
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether any dependency the repository declares is published as MALICIOUS rather than merely vulnerable — a package that is an attacker's work, in any ecosystem osv-scanner reads. Scored apart from D30 because the answer is binary: there is no safe version to upgrade to, and the fix is to remove the package and rotate every credential it could have read.

dimensions.name: Platform End-of-Life
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether anyone still ships security patches for the platform this repository RUNS ON — the runtime it pins and the framework majors its own constraints hold it to. Separate from D12 because the question differs: a current Django on an end-of-life Python is perfectly up to date and completely unsupported, and the fix is a migration rather than a version bump. What the repository says it merely SUPPORTS is never charged.

dimensions.name: Text alternatives
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether non-text content carries a text alternative — img/area/input[type=image] have alt, a meaningful svg has a title or aria-label, video has a captions track, and object/embed/canvas have a name or fallback content. Static markup readiness, not a WCAG conformance claim.

dimensions.name: Forms & labels
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether form controls have a programmatic label (an associated label, aria-label or aria-labelledby), buttons have text, links have an accessible name, a click handler on a plain element names the control it declares, fieldsets have a non-empty legend, known UI-library field components carry a label prop, and a placeholder isn't used as the only label. Static markup readiness, not a WCAG conformance claim.

dimensions.name: Page structure
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether pages declare a language (well-formed BCP-47) and a non-empty title, expose exactly one main landmark and a sane heading order with non-empty headings, keep zoom enabled, title their iframes, give data tables header cells, and avoid meta-refresh. Static markup readiness, not a WCAG conformance claim.

dimensions.name: Keyboard semantics
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether interactive behaviour is keyboard-reachable — no click handler on a non-interactive element lacking a role, tabindex and key handler, no element the repo's own CSS styles `cursor: pointer` without giving it any of the three, no unfocusable element whose only binding is a mouse enter/leave pair or a double-click, no positive tabindex, no href-less anchor, no placeholder-href (#/javascript) link acting as a button. Static markup readiness, not a WCAG conformance claim.

dimensions.name: ARIA correctness
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether ARIA is used correctly — valid non-abstract roles, the ARIA state a role requires, valid (non-misspelled) aria-* attribute names, in-enum values for token-typed aria-* attributes, and no aria-hidden on (or wrapping) a focusable element. Static markup readiness, not a WCAG conformance claim.

dimensions.name: Visual & motion safety
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether focus outlines aren't removed without a replacement, motion respects prefers-reduced-motion, and literal CSS colour pairs meet contrast — PARTIAL: inline styles, in-repo <style> blocks, in-repo .css files, var() tokens, Tailwind neutral utilities and CSS-in-JS literals are read (hex/rgb/hsl/named), never computed/runtime/external-CDN colour. Static markup readiness, not a WCAG conformance claim.

dimensions.name: A11y enforcement
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether accessibility is ENFORCED in the toolchain — an accessibility checker configured over the markup (an a11y lint rule set, e.g. eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y or vuejs-accessibility where the project lints JavaScript) and an automated accessibility assertion wired into tests or CI (axe/pa11y/Lighthouse or an equivalent) — on the Documented→Verified→Prevented ladder.

dimensions.name: Captive dependencies
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether any singleton service captures a scoped/transient dependency — a silent lifetime/threading bug.

dimensions.name: Stateful singletons
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether singleton services avoid mutable shared instance state that concurrent callers would race on.

dimensions.name: Project dependency cycles
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the project-reference graph is acyclic (cycles block independent build/deploy and signal eroding boundaries).

dimensions.name: Dependency direction
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether dependencies point inward (Domain ← Application ← Infrastructure/Web) — the clean-architecture dependency rule, checked across the project graph.

dimensions.name: Architecture & structure
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the codebase has a recognisable, scale-appropriate structure (a named architectural style, or modular enough for its size) rather than being an ad-hoc ball of mud.

dimensions.name: Interface segregation
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether interfaces stay focused rather than fat — the Interface-Segregation principle (SOLID 'I').

dimensions.name: Slice cohesion
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether feature slices stay independent (no direct cross-slice references) — the discipline that makes vertical-slice architecture pay off.

dimensions.name: Test isolation
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether production projects stay free of references to test projects — tests may depend on production, never the reverse.

dimensions.name: CQS / query purity
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether read (query) handlers stay side-effect-free — a query that writes persistent state or raises events breaks CQS and makes reads unsafe to retry, cache, or route to a read replica.

dimensions.name: Code composition
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How the codebase splits by code ROLE — domain, application, infrastructure, test, generated. The significance map behind the knowledge/coupling weighting, and a DDD signal in its own right: a thin domain core under fat infrastructure is the anemic-domain smell, quantified.

dimensions.name: Runtime unauthenticated reachability
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Of the screens reached by crawling with the application's own logged-in session, which ones also answer a GET carrying no credentials. Observed on the live app; GET only, and only URLs the crawl already fetched. Advisory; never scored.

dimensions.name: Runtime evidence locked — no reproducible boot
dimensions.whatItMeasures: The Runtime Evidence tier found no declared way to boot this app (docker-compose, Aspire AppHost, or a Dockerfile), so no live runtime a11y/egress/header evidence was gathered. Advisory — never affects the CAI score.

dimensions.name: Runtime readiness
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How reproducibly this app can be booted for runtime evidence, plus the test frameworks detected. Advisory — never affects the score.

dimensions.name: Runtime security headers
dimensions.whatItMeasures: HTTP security headers the live app actually set, observed by booting it in our no-coupling sandbox — advisory evidence for AppSec / CRA / NIS2 runtime secure-defaults. Never scored.

dimensions.name: Runtime container hardening
dimensions.whatItMeasures: The confinement each container was actually started with — effective user, privileged mode, added and dropped capabilities, read-only root filesystem, no-new-privileges — read from the running stack rather than from a Dockerfile. Advisory; never scored.

dimensions.name: Runtime cookie security
dimensions.whatItMeasures: The HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite flags on the cookies the live application actually issued, read from its own responses. Advisory; never scored.

dimensions.name: Runtime API surface
dimensions.whatItMeasures: The API description the running application serves about itself, diffed against the one the repository commits, plus anonymous GET probes of its parameter-free operations. Templated paths and non-GET methods are listed as surface and never requested. Advisory; never scored.

dimensions.name: Runtime third-party data flows
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Third-party hosts the rendered UI tried to reach (analytics/trackers/CDNs), observed at render time — advisory evidence for GDPR data-protection-by-default. Never scored; jurisdiction/role never inferred.

dimensions.name: Runtime accessibility (rendered)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: WCAG success criteria verified in a real headless-browser render (axe-core), double-render checked and kept as advisory evidence — never scored.

dimensions.name: Runtime exposed surface
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Every network binding the application actually opened when booted in our no-coupling sandbox — service, container port, host port, protocol and bind scope — with any port the repository's own files never declare called out. Observed, never inferred from a manifest. Advisory; never scored.

dimensions.name: Data Protection
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether sensitive data is encrypted at rest and in transit and keys are vaulted.

dimensions.name: Access Controls
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether access is authorized by default — a framework authorization attribute/decorator or policy, or imperative guard methods (throw-on-violation) called from handlers.

dimensions.name: Audit Trail
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether changes to sensitive data are recorded (who, what, when) for compliance + incident response.

dimensions.name: Data Retention
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether data has a defined lifetime — retention periods, TTLs, cleanup jobs (storage limitation).

dimensions.name: Data-Subject Rights
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether GDPR data-subject requests are supported in code — erasure, export/portability, consent.

dimensions.name: Aggregate boundaries
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether aggregates reference each other by identity (id) rather than by direct object reference — the core DDD consistency-boundary rule.

dimensions.name: Strongly-typed ids
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How much of the domain uses strongly-typed ids vs raw Guid/string/int — adoption curve, not all-or-nothing.

dimensions.name: Integration-event coupling
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether cross-context integration events stay loosely coupled — no producer-owned enums/domain types leaking to consumers. Shared-kernel/contracts types are allowed.

dimensions.name: Rich vs anemic model
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether aggregates/entities carry the behaviour that protects their invariants, rather than being data bags driven by external services.

dimensions.name: Encapsulated state
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether entities protect their state (private/init-only setters) instead of exposing public setters that bypass invariants. Softened when a rehydration framework (Marten/EF) is present.

dimensions.name: Domain ↔ infrastructure boundary
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the domain layer stays free of infrastructure dependencies (EF/Marten/HTTP/ASP.NET) — the clean-architecture dependency rule.

dimensions.name: Repository granularity
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether repositories are per aggregate root (not per child entity) so the root's invariants can't be bypassed.

dimensions.name: Value-object opportunities
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether clusters of primitives that travel together (a missing value object) are extracted — a low-weight suggestion, LLM-confirmed when configured.

dimensions.name: Scattered domain decisions
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether one domain rule is decided — or one measurement produced — in more than one place, rather than living on the type that owns it. A repeated judgement or a repeated derivation, not repeated text, so a clone detector cannot see either; and centralising the judgement does not fix the derivation, because two producers of the same numbers can disagree while every rule reading them is correct.

dimensions.name: One transaction, one aggregate
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a single operation mutates more than one aggregate root. An aggregate is a consistency boundary, so saving two together fuses them into one — the second's invariants come to depend on the first's transaction, and the pair can no longer be separated. Reads of other aggregates are not counted.

dimensions.name: Constructible invalid state
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether an aggregate can be constructed in a state its own rules forbid — a public constructor that takes a raw primitive, stores it, and validates nothing, with no factory beside it. A constructor taking only value objects is not counted: each parameter has already validated itself.

dimensions.name: Ambient inputs in the domain
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether domain types receive the time and randomness their rules depend on, rather than reading the process clock or a global random source directly — an ambient read makes the rule it feeds untestable at the instant that matters and lets two reads inside one operation disagree.

dimensions.name: Handler temporal coupling
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether event handlers stay asynchronous (no blocking remote HTTP/gRPC calls awaited inside a handler).

dimensions.name: Event/command shape
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether commands have a single handler (one owner of the decision) and fan-out is modelled with events.

dimensions.name: Event naming
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether events are named in the past tense (a clarity nudge — low weight).

dimensions.name: Outbox / dual-write
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether state changes and message publishes are atomic (a transactional outbox) rather than a crash-unsafe dual write.

dimensions.name: Idempotency
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether retry-prone mutations (command handlers + message/event consumers) are idempotent so an at-least-once redelivery or client retry doesn't double-apply the effect — heuristic at-risk detection confirmed by language model, advisory.

dimensions.name: Fold determinism
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether Apply/When folds reconstruct state purely from the event (no DateTime.Now, Guid.NewGuid, Random or IO) so replay is reproducible.

dimensions.name: Immutable events
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether persisted events are immutable facts (init-only/readonly) — a settable event member lets stored history be rewritten.

dimensions.name: PII in the event store
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the append-only event log avoids un-erasable personal data (or has a crypto-shredding strategy) — a GDPR right-to-erasure risk.

dimensions.name: Unfinished & placeholder code
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Unreviewed-generation residue: shipped members still throwing NotImplementedException, and placeholder string literals left in non-test, non-generated code. Scored as a quality signature, never as a claim about authorship.

dimensions.name: Incompleteness & stubs
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Unfinished work detected by code SHAPE, not keywords: members that only throw a "not implemented" exception, methods that take inputs and return a constant, async methods that never await, dead `if (false)` / `#if false` branches, and skeleton types most of whose members are holes. A real, objective slice of technical debt.

dimensions.name: Personal-Data Handling (GDPR)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: LLM-confirmed personal-data handling surface — fields that are genuine personal data about a real person (not fiction/test/config), surfaced for the GDPR Art. 25/32 self-assessment. Advisory.

dimensions.name: Alt-Text Quality (WCAG 1.1.1)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: LLM-judged quality of image alt text — whether each alt is a meaningful equivalent rather than a filename, generic word or placeholder. Advisory; complements the deterministic 'alt present?' check.

dimensions.name: Vulnerability-Disclosure Policy
dimensions.whatItMeasures: LLM-judged whether a SECURITY.md / security.txt is a real coordinated vulnerability-disclosure policy (contact + how to report + handling), not just a stub. Advisory.

dimensions.name: Dev/Test/Prod Separation
dimensions.whatItMeasures: LLM-judged whether configuration separates development/test/production (distinct per-environment settings) rather than commingling them. Advisory.

dimensions.name: Link & Button Text Quality (WCAG 2.4.4)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: LLM-judged descriptiveness of link/button text — whether each conveys its purpose out of context rather than a vague 'click here'/'read more'. Advisory; complements the deterministic 'has a name?' check.

dimensions.name: Heading & Label Text Quality (WCAG 2.4.6)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: LLM-judged descriptiveness of heading/label text — whether each meaningfully describes its section or field rather than a placeholder ('Heading', 'Untitled', 'Label'). Advisory.

dimensions.name: Documentation (README)
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the repo and its projects have a README, and whether it's substantive and current.

dimensions.name: Architecture documentation
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether key decisions (ADRs) and the high-level shape (C4/diagrams) are written down.

dimensions.name: Folder & project structure
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the repo is organised deliberately — src/test separation and consistent project naming.

dimensions.name: Documentation accuracy
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the README actually describes the code that exists (LLM-judged, advisory).

dimensions.name: CI/CD gates
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether an automated pipeline builds and tests every change.

dimensions.name: Observability
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the code is diagnosable in production — structured logging, tracing/metrics, health checks.

dimensions.name: Security & performance tooling
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether SAST, secret/dependency scanning and performance benchmarking are wired in (presence, not runtime).

dimensions.name: Deployment & Rollback
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether releases are automated and safely reversible (probes, rolling updates, approval gates) — from manifests/pipeline files, not the live environment.

dimensions.name: DR & Backup
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether disaster recovery is planned and codified — backups, geo-recovery, RTO/RPO, persistence guarantees — from IaC + container manifests + docs, never the live cloud.

dimensions.name: Release Hygiene
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether releases are traceable — a maintained changelog and explicit version stamping.

dimensions.name: Outbound HTTP resilience
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether outbound HTTP calls are wrapped in resilience (retry/timeout/circuit-breaker) so a failing dependency doesn't cascade.

dimensions.name: Schema migrations
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether database schema changes go through versioned migrations rather than being auto-created from the model (EF Core EnsureCreated(), GORM AutoMigrate, SQLAlchemy create_all, TypeORM synchronize, Hibernate ddl-auto).

dimensions.name: Domain vs controller coverage
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether test coverage concentrates on the domain (business rules) rather than the trivial web/controller layer — a focus check a generic tool can't make.

dimensions.name: Library API & versioning
dimensions.whatItMeasures: For a library: a deliberate (small) public API surface and explicit semantic versioning so consumers can depend on it safely.

dimensions.name: BDD / executable specs
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether behaviour is captured as executable Gherkin specifications (a plus for shared understanding) — only assessed when a BDD framework is present.

dimensions.name: CI test-gate honesty
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the CI gate executes the test inventory it appears to have: excluded suites, skipped tests, and coverage collected without a threshold.

dimensions.name: Benchmark discipline
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the code protects its performance with benchmarks — a benchmark suite, allocation/memory measurement, and (ideally) a CI gate. Presence is credited as a bonus, never a deduction.

dimensions.name: Allocation hygiene
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the code is written to minimise allocations so it doesn't pressure its host's memory manager — buffer/slice views over copies, object pooling, stack or value-type allocation, and buffer writers. Reward-only: credited where present, never penalised where a simpler style is fine.

dimensions.name: Async & latency hygiene
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether asynchronous code stays responsive — it avoids sync-over-async blocking (a .NET .Wait()/.GetAwaiter().GetResult(), a time.sleep or blocking HTTP call inside a Python coroutine, a *Sync call inside an async JavaScript function, block_on inside a Rust async fn, runBlocking inside a Kotlin suspend function, block() inside a Reactor publisher) that stalls a thread or event loop and risks deadlock, and, where the code is a reusable library on .NET, awaits with ConfigureAwait(false) so it never captures and stalls its caller's context.

dimensions.name: Type Safety
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How much of the frontend is typed TypeScript vs untyped JavaScript.

dimensions.name: Cyclomatic Complexity
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Per-function cyclomatic/cognitive complexity from the token-level function scanner (D-386) — real branching, not a regex heuristic.

dimensions.name: Large Files
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How many source files exceed the large-file threshold.

dimensions.name: Test Coverage
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Static test reachability (D-386): the share of production files reachable from any test via the import graph — measured without running anything.

dimensions.name: Dependency Freshness
dimensions.whatItMeasures: How outdated the npm dependencies are (a maturity signal). JS/npm CVEs are scored separately in D30 (JS/npm Dependency Vulnerabilities).

dimensions.name: Tooling
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the project wires up test, lint and typecheck — detected from each package.json script's COMMAND (eslint / tsc / vitest / jest / playwright), not just its name, and corroborated against CI-workflow invocations so a tool run only in CI still counts.

dimensions.name: Dead Code
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Files unreachable from every application/tooling/test entry point, and exports nothing imports (module-graph reachability, D-386).

dimensions.name: Dependency Hygiene
dimensions.whatItMeasures: npm dependency truthfulness (D-386): unused dependencies, imports not declared anywhere, and type-/test-only packages shipped as production deps.

dimensions.name: Circular Imports
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Import cycles in the module graph (D-386) — files that can only be understood and changed together.

dimensions.name: Code Duplication
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Near-exact copy-pasted blocks of substantial extent across the frontend (the D4 clone algorithm over JS/TS tokens, D-386): a block is reported only where its copies still agree on most of their own identifiers and literals, or were renamed as they were pasted but kept most of their constants, and where the copies carry enough code to stand on their own or the copied extent reaches 30 lines — so a re-implementation sharing neither names nor values, and a small pasted declaration, are both found and deliberately not reported, and a clean R10 is not a claim that nothing was copied.

dimensions.name: Import Boundaries
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Conformance to the detected frontend architecture layout (feature-sliced / layered src) plus cross-package deep-import rules (D-386).

dimensions.name: Web-Security Posture
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Transport security, security headers, secure cookies, input validation, middleware order and crypto hygiene (presence, not runtime).

dimensions.name: Supply-chain hygiene
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Reproducible, pinned builds (SSDF PW.4 / SLSA): dependency lockfiles + the deny-by-default egress sandbox the build runs in (it can fetch only from allow-listed registries — build-time provenance). Advisory; never scored.

dimensions.name: Async correctness
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the code avoids sync-over-async (deadlock-prone blocking on tasks) and async void.

dimensions.name: Cancellation propagation
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether async methods accept a CancellationToken so work can be cancelled (adoption curve).

dimensions.name: Exception handling
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether exceptions are handled rather than silently swallowed or rethrown with lost stack traces.

dimensions.name: Structured logging
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether log calls use message templates (queryable) rather than interpolated strings.

dimensions.name: Nullable reference types
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether nullable reference types are enabled and not undermined by heavy `!` suppression.

dimensions.name: Hand-rolled structured-format parsing
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether JSON/XML is parsed with regex/string hacks while a real parser is already referenced in the same project — a classic source of silent data bugs.

dimensions.name: Silent fallback defaults
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether parse/lookup failure paths return hard-coded constants with no logging or throw — failures that convert data errors into silent behavior changes.

dimensions.name: JS interop contract
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether string-named JS interop bindings resolve against the first-party JavaScript, and whether anything guards the boundary against renames.

dimensions.name: Subsumed condition operand
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether any `||`/`&&` operand logically implies another in the same chain, making it dead — the expression means something wider (or narrower) than it reads.

dimensions.name: Duplicated predicate
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether one non-trivial boolean expression is written out character-identically in two or more files — a single-line clone the token-window duplication detector cannot see.

dimensions.name: Unreachable branch
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether any branch is dead by construction — a switch arm whose label can never equal a case-normalised subject, or an `else if` whose predicate the arm above has already swallowed.

dimensions.name: Undrained process stream
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a child process with BOTH standard streams redirected drains both — reading one to the end while the other is never read deadlocks once the child fills the unread pipe.

dimensions.name: Bypassable address classification
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a hand-rolled public/private IP check can be walked past — a method that unwraps IPv4-mapped IPv6 but returns the opposite verdict for the same host written as IPv4-compatible, 6to4 or NAT64.

dimensions.name: Unvalidated length from an untrusted reader
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a length read out of the stream being parsed is bounded before it is allocated or read — an unchecked count taken from the input lets the input choose the allocation.

dimensions.name: Unfloored truncation loop
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a loop that shortens a string until it fits a length budget has a floor — one with none grinds the value down to the empty string, or past it into a negative-length `Substring`.

dimensions.name: Uncapped recursion over a caller-supplied document
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a walk that recurses through a JSON/XML tree handed in by its caller bounds how deep it will go — an uncapped walk lets the document's nesting choose the stack depth, and the resulting StackOverflowException cannot be caught.

dimensions.name: Disposal-pattern correctness
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a type's disposal matches what it OWNS — releasing what it created, leaving alone what it was handed, and not declaring a finalizer for state that has nothing unmanaged to finalize.

dimensions.name: Unrestored process-global state
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a method that temporarily changes state belonging to the whole process — the working directory, an environment variable — puts it back on EVERY path: a restore reached only when nothing throws leaks the change to the rest of the process.

dimensions.name: Mistyped argument guard
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether an argument guard throws the exception its own condition describes — a guard that rejects a value for being EMPTY and reports it as `ArgumentNullException` tells the caller a parameter was null when it provably was not.

dimensions.name: Side-effecting pattern guard
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a `when` guard is free of side effects — a guard that increments a counter or assigns while deciding whether its arm matches applies that change during PATTERN MATCHING, on an arm that may not be selected, and skips it entirely when a short-circuit to its left answers first.

dimensions.name: Contradicted release guard
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a method that TAKES a lock or semaphore and gives it back from a flag-guarded `finally` returns the value that flag implies — reporting success while the guard hands the primitive back admits a second caller the exclusion was there to keep out, and reporting failure while the guard keeps it leaves nothing to ever give it back.

dimensions.name: Unguarded diagnostic materialisation
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether the work a diagnostic log line costs is paid only when that line is wanted — C# evaluates a call's arguments BEFORE the call, so a trace/debug message joined or projected out of a collection is built in full on every pass, and then discarded by a sink the shipped configuration leaves switched off.

dimensions.name: Document value interpolated into markup unescaped
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether text read out of the document being converted is escaped before it is written into generated markup — a value the document's author chose, interpolated into an attribute the surrounding literal delimits, can close that attribute and open another.

dimensions.name: Inert configuration knob
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a value the caller is invited to supply is the value the type actually uses — a constructor parameter stored in a private field that nothing ever reads while the default it was given is spelled out a second time at the site that should have read it, a keyed lookup that falls back to a different setting than the one its key names while the same type falls back to the matching one for that same key, or a culture-sensitive parse given no format provider by a type that feeds its own settable culture to the same kind of parse elsewhere. Either way, every caller who supplies a value silently gets something else.

dimensions.name: Unsynchronised callback handoff
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a value handed from a callback to the body that waits on it crosses on something built to be crossed — a `Queue<T>`/`List<T>`/`Dictionary<K,V>` written inside an event handler and read back outside it is mutated by two flows at once, and the semaphore or completion source beside it orders how MANY items exist while leaving the collection's own head, tail and backing array unprotected.

dimensions.name: Collection changed while being enumerated
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a `foreach` leaves the collection it is walking alone — a body that adds to or removes from the very collection the loop is enumerating invalidates the enumerator it is holding, so the next `MoveNext` throws `InvalidOperationException` and the remaining items are never seen.

dimensions.name: Index access outside its own emptiness guard
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a condition that tests a value for emptiness indexes that same value only where the test holds — an `||` written one parenthesis too far to the left leaves an index access outside the guard beside it, so the empty case the guard exists to anticipate reaches the index and throws instead.

dimensions.name: Per-element action decided by a fixed element
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a decision taken once per element is taken ABOUT that element — a test inside a counted loop that reads a fixed subscript of the very collection its guarded statement indexes by the loop variable applies element zero's answer to all of them, so the elements that differ from it are all handled wrongly, and in the same direction.

dimensions.name: Support guard that admits what it rejects
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a guard written as a NEGATED `||` says what its author meant — `!(a || b || x != k)` is `!a && !b && x == k` by De Morgan, so a bail-out that mixes capabilities the code needs with a fault it refuses turns inside out: it fires only where the capabilities are ABSENT, and lets every value the fault term names walk straight into the body that cannot handle it.

dimensions.name: Test-only surface in a production module
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a production module publishes functions that exist only for its tests — Erlang has no visibility below `-export`, so a test helper exported unconditionally becomes part of the module's contract for every caller in the system, and the `-ifdef(TEST)` idiom that would keep it out of the shipped module is not used.

dimensions.name: Type resolved by simple name across every loaded assembly
dimensions.whatItMeasures: Whether a plugin lookup names the type it means — searching every assembly loaded into the process for a candidate whose SIMPLE name equals a string supplied at runtime, and taking the first one found, is decided by assembly LOAD ORDER rather than by this source, so the same name can resolve to a different type on the next run.
